narrative.text: The excavation for the new library building has stopped. The workers found bones. Not ancient bones — bones with bullet holes. A mass grave. The BNI archives identify the site as an unrecorded execution ground used during the 1947 purges. Among the remains: personal effects that identify some of the dead. Dissidents. Journalists. Teachers. People who spoke against Halvek and disappeared.

This is a war crime site. We cannot build a library on top of it as if nothing happened. I recommend we halt construction, create a memorial, and relocate the library to an alternative site on campus. It will cost more — perhaps eight million ₭ — and delay the project. But the alternative is building a house of learning on top of a house of murder.
I am going to report this regardless of what you decide. The question is whether I report that the Chancellor honored the dead — or that she buried them a second time.

choices.text: "Halt construction. Create a memorial. The dead of 1947 will not be paved over. This university will honor them — and every student who walks past that memorial will know what was done here and why it must never be done again."

"Document the remains. Give them a proper burial elsewhere. Then continue construction. The library will serve thousands of students for generations — that is its own kind of memorial. We honor the dead by building the future they died for."
